evals.prompt: Our on-call rotation now includes engineers in Poland and India, and two of them told me our runbooks are hard to parse at 3am. Can you rewrite evals/fixtures/keda-runbook.md in Simplified Technical English? Keep every technical detail — the queue name, the 14-day retention, the page-the-platform-team rule — I just need it unambiguous. Save it next to the original as keda-runbook.ste.md and tell me what you changed.
evals.expected_output: The runbook rewritten in ASD-STE100 STE: numbered imperative steps of 20 words or fewer, descriptive prose of 25 words or fewer, active voice, no semicolons, no contractions, no Latin abbreviations, unapproved words replaced (ensure -> make sure, verify -> make sure, should -> must, executing -> use/do, i.e. -> that is, however -> but, therefore -> thus/as a result, rotate -> change). The NOTE containing an instruction must become a work step or a safety instruction, because a note gives information only (Rule 5.5). The purge-the-queue consequence should be a CAUTION or WARNING with a stated result (Rules 7.1-7.3). Every fact preserved: profile-enrichment queue, /profiles/:id endpoint, CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, maxReplicaCount, ClusterTriggerAuthentication, the New Relic alert policy name quoted exactly, 14-day retention. Code, commands, identifiers and quoted strings left verbatim. A short change table listing rule, before and after.

assertions.text: Runs the bundled checker on its own output
assertions.passing_criteria: The transcript shows scripts/ste_check.py invoked against the rewritten file (not only against the input), and the reported errors were fixed

assertions.text: Rewritten file has zero checker errors
assertions.passing_criteria: python3 scripts/ste_check.py on the produced file exits 0 with 0 error findings

assertions.text: No procedural sentence is longer than 20 STE words
assertions.passing_criteria: Every numbered or bulleted instruction in the output is 20 words or fewer under the STE counting rules 8.4 thru 8.7 (parentheticals, numbers with units, abbreviations, identifiers, quoted text and hyphenated groups each count as one word)

assertions.text: Replaces the recurring unapproved words
assertions.passing_criteria: The output contains no instance of ensure, verify, should, may, however, therefore, i.e., e.g., utilize, perform, execute, or a semicolon, and uses the approved alternatives instead (make sure, must, but, thus/as a result, that is, use, do)

assertions.text: Turns the instruction-bearing NOTE into a step or safety instruction
assertions.passing_criteria: The 'Always page the platform team' content appears as a numbered work step or as a WARNING/CAUTION, not as a NOTE, per Rule 5.5

assertions.text: States a consequence for the destructive action
assertions.passing_criteria: The queue-purge content appears as a WARNING or CAUTION that names the result (the messages are erased and cannot be recovered), satisfying Rules 7.1 thru 7.3

assertions.text: Preserves every technical fact
assertions.passing_criteria: The output still contains the queue name profile-enrichment, the /profiles/:id endpoint, CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, maxReplicaCount, ClusterTriggerAuthentication, the 14-day retention period, and the New Relic alert policy name — none dropped, none altered

assertions.text: Leaves commands and quoted strings unchanged
assertions.passing_criteria: kubectl get pods -n consumer-profile appears verbatim and no code, command, identifier or quoted label was reworded to satisfy the dictionary

assertions.text: Reports the changes
assertions.passing_criteria: The response includes a table or list of the substantive rewrites with the rule number, the original text and the STE text

evals.prompt: Before I send evals/fixtures/migration-doc.md to the Data Platform team for sign-off, is it STE compliant? Don't rewrite the whole thing — I want to know what's actually wrong with it, per rule, so the author can fix it themselves.
evals.expected_output: A compliance audit report, not a rewrite: verdict with an error count, a per-rule summary table, findings anchored to file:line with the offending text and a suggested STE correction, a section for the items that need a human decision (candidate technical nouns such as warehouse, dynamic table, resource monitor, and past participles that may be adjectives), and a section naming what the document already gets right. Findings must cite real rule numbers: 3.4 (has been tested, has not been executed), 3.6 (was suspended by the resource monitor, will be required), 3.5 (utilizing, running, in progress), 8.1 (three semicolons), 1.1 (ensure, utilizing, should, may, therefore, retried, concurrently, e.g., approximately usage), GR-6 (e.g.), 6.3 (the 60-plus-word closing sentence), 5.5/7.1 (the do-not-run-twice consequence belongs in a WARNING or CAUTION). The audit must not reword the SQL block or the quoted Snowflake error string.

assertions.text: Produces an audit, not a rewrite
assertions.passing_criteria: The output is a findings report with a verdict and per-rule findings; it does not deliver a wholesale rewritten version of the document

assertions.text: Uses the checker rather than estimating
assertions.passing_criteria: The transcript shows scripts/ste_check.py run against the fixture, and the report's counts are consistent with the checker output

assertions.text: Findings cite specific ASD-STE100 rule numbers
assertions.passing_criteria: At least six distinct rule identifiers appear (for example 1.1, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 5.5, 6.3, 7.1, 8.1, GR-6), each attached to the text it applies to

assertions.text: Catches the perfect-tense and passive constructions
assertions.passing_criteria: The report flags 'has been tested' / 'has not yet been executed' under Rule 3.4 and at least one passive construction such as 'was suspended by the resource monitor' under Rule 3.6

assertions.text: Catches both prose semicolons and spares the one in the SQL
assertions.passing_criteria: The report flags the semicolon on line 5 and the one on line 15 under Rule 8.1 and locates them by line, and does not flag the semicolon that terminates the CALL statement inside the fenced SQL block

assertions.text: Flags the over-length sentence with the correct limit
assertions.passing_criteria: The final paragraph's long sentence is flagged against the 25-word descriptive limit (Rule 6.3), not against the 20-word procedural limit

assertions.text: Anchors findings to lines
assertions.passing_criteria: Findings reference the file and line number (or quote the exact offending text) so the author can locate each one

assertions.text: Separates judgment calls from proven breaches
assertions.passing_criteria: The report distinguishes provable errors from items needing a human decision — candidate technical nouns (Rule 1.5) or a past participle that may be an adjective (Rule 3.3) — rather than presenting all findings as violations

assertions.text: Does not demand changes to code or quoted text
assertions.passing_criteria: The report does not ask for the SQL statement or the quoted error string 'Error: 000603 (57014): SQL execution canceled' to be reworded, per Rule 8.6

evals.prompt: I need to write the safety section for a new internal CLI we ship to agents' laptops. The `eq-sync reset` command wipes the local cache and re-downloads it; if the laptop loses Wi-Fi partway through, the cache ends up half-written and the agent sees stale quotes until they run it again. Also the command needs a confirmation prompt they have to type the environment name into. Write this up in simplified technical english for the docs — a warning plus the steps.
evals.expected_output: New STE text written from raw notes, not a rewrite: a CAUTION (risk of damage to data/objects, not injury) that starts with the command or the condition and states the consequence (Rules 7.1 thru 7.3), plus numbered imperative steps of 20 words or fewer with one instruction each. Conditions come before commands (Rule 5.4). Approved vocabulary throughout — 'make sure', 'must', 'erase'/'remove' rather than wipe, 'get again'/'download' for re-download, no 'ensure', no 'should', no contractions, no Latin abbreviations. The command name, the typed environment name and any quoted prompt text stay verbatim. The stale-quote consequence must be stated as a result the reader can act on, and the half-written cache condition must be named as the trigger.

assertions.text: Uses a caution or warning with a stated consequence
assertions.passing_criteria: The output contains a CAUTION or WARNING that names the risk level, starts with a command or a condition, and states the result (a half-written cache, stale quotes) per Rules 7.1 thru 7.3

assertions.text: Steps are imperative with one instruction each
assertions.passing_criteria: Every numbered step is in the command form and contains a single instruction, unless two actions genuinely occur at the same time (Rules 5.2, 5.3)

assertions.text: Every procedural sentence is 20 STE words or fewer
assertions.passing_criteria: No step exceeds 20 words counted per rules 8.4 thru 8.7

assertions.text: Zero checker errors
assertions.passing_criteria: python3 scripts/ste_check.py on the produced text reports 0 error findings

assertions.text: Condition precedes the command
assertions.passing_criteria: Where a condition applies (network loss, environment confirmation), the descriptive condition comes first, separated from the command by a comma, per Rule 5.4

assertions.text: Keeps the command and prompt text verbatim
assertions.passing_criteria: eq-sync reset appears exactly as given, and any confirmation prompt text is quoted rather than paraphrased into approved words

assertions.text: No unapproved vocabulary in the prose
assertions.passing_criteria: The output avoids ensure, should, may, wipe, e.g., i.e., contractions and semicolons, using approved alternatives instead

assertions.text: Explains the STE choices it made
assertions.passing_criteria: The response says why it chose a caution rather than a warning (risk to data, not injury) or otherwise shows the rule reasoning, rather than silently producing text

evals.prompt: quick one — can you STE-ify this line for our status page? "We are currently experiencing elevated error rates on the quote submission API; our engineers have identified the root cause and are actively working on a fix, and we will provide an update shortly."
evals.expected_output: A short STE rewrite of one sentence, correctly handled as descriptive text (status update, not instructions, so no imperative form and the 25-word limit applies). The three banned constructions must all go: the progressive forms 'are currently experiencing' / 'are actively working' (Rule 3.2, 3.5), the present perfect 'have identified' (Rule 3.4), and the semicolon (Rule 8.1). Unapproved words replaced: currently, experiencing, elevated, actively, shortly, provide, root cause. Result should be two or three short sentences that keep every fact — which API, that the cause is known, that a fix is in progress, that another update follows — and should give the reader a concrete next-update time or say plainly that the time is not known, because 'shortly' is not information. No invented facts such as a made-up percentage or timestamp.

assertions.text: Treats the text as descriptive, not procedural
assertions.passing_criteria: The rewrite uses no imperative form and is judged against the 25-word descriptive limit (Rule 6.3)

assertions.text: Removes the progressive and perfect constructions
assertions.passing_criteria: No '-ing' verb forms after a form of 'to be' and no 'have/has + past participle' remain (Rules 3.2, 3.4, 3.5)

assertions.text: Removes the semicolon
assertions.passing_criteria: The output contains no semicolon and instead uses separate sentences (Rule 8.1)

assertions.text: Replaces the unapproved words
assertions.passing_criteria: currently, experiencing, elevated, actively, shortly, provide and root cause are all gone, replaced with approved words or a different construction

assertions.text: Keeps all four facts
assertions.passing_criteria: The rewrite still says which API is affected, that error rates are high, that the cause is known, that a repair is in progress, and that another report will follow. Accept the approved-word equivalents rather than the original wording — STE says 'repair' for 'fix' and 'report'/'tell' for 'update', so grading must not require the unapproved words.

assertions.text: Invents no new facts
assertions.passing_criteria: No specific error percentage, incident number, duration or timestamp appears that was not in the input; if a next-update time is recommended, it is flagged as something the author must fill in

assertions.text: Stays proportionate to a one-line request
assertions.passing_criteria: The response leads with the rewritten text and keeps any rule explanation brief — it does not produce a full audit report or a multi-section document for a single sentence
